newsitem.title: CANADA: Noranda board okays C$212 mln in projects.
newsitem.headline: Noranda board okays C$212 mln in projects.

text.p: Noranda Inc said on Wednesday its board approved five mining and minerals capital projects totalling C$212 million.

"These projects, which will be carried out over the next two years, will increase the production capacity and the productivity of Noranda copper and zinc operations, and will increase the company's profitability," Noranda said.
In its copper operations, Noranda will invest C$142 million to boost smelting capacity and to modernize its refining operations.
Of the C$142 million, C$124 million will be invested at Noranda Metallurgy's 360,000 tonne a year CCR refinery in Montreal East, Quebec, to introduce permanent cathode technology.

At the Gaspe copper smelter at Murdochville, Quebec, Noranda will invest C$18 million to build a third converter that will increase the treatment capacity by more than 15 percent to reach 350,000 tonnes a year.
The new converter will allow an increase of 16,000 tonnes in copper anode production.
Noranda will invest C$70 million in three zinc projects to raise capacity and competitiveness.
At the Canadian Electrolytic Zinc refinery in Valleyfield, Quebec, Noranda will allocate C$32 million to increase annual production capacity by 11 percent to 250,000 tonnes of zinc.
Another C$29 million will be invested at the refinery to permit the implementation of a process developed with the Noranda Technology Centre for the disposal and treatment of the production residues.
This new process represents a first in the North American zinc industry.

Noranda will also reopen an open pit zinc mine, Mine Gallen, situated near Rouyn-Noranda. The reopening of this operation will cost C$9 million and will allow Noranda to produce 82,000 tonnes of zinc concentrate at the Horne Smelter during 18 months of operation.
